summary.text: Marilyn Strickland is the Democratic incumbent for Washington's 10th Congressional District. Born in Seoul and raised in Tacoma, she served as mayor of Tacoma and as president and CEO of the Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce before her 2020 election to Congress. She serves on the House Armed Services and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and is running for re-election.

paragraphs.text: Born September 25, 1962, in Seoul, South Korea; her family moved to Tacoma in 1967 after her father, a U.S. serviceman, was stationed at Fort Lewis, and she was raised in Tacoma and attended Mount Tahoma High School. Her campaign website describes her as an "Army brat" and a graduate of Tacoma Public Schools.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Washington and a master's degree in business administration from Clark Atlanta University.
Worked in the private sector, including at Northern Life Insurance, before entering local government; was later a member of the Tacoma City Council.

Served as mayor of Tacoma from 2010 to 2018 (two terms, according to her campaign website); Wikipedia describes her as the city's first Asian-born elected mayor and first African-American woman in the office.
After her mayoralty, served as president and CEO of the Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce.

Elected to Congress in November 2020 and sworn in January 3, 2021. According to her campaign website she is the first African-American and Korean-American woman elected to Congress; her House website says she is the first African American to represent Washington state in federal office.

For the 119th Congress (2025-2026), sits on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Subcommittee on Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation; Subcommittee on Highways and Transit) and the House Committee on Armed Services (Subcommittee on Military Personnel; Subcommittee on Readiness).
Her House website lists her as Whip of the New Democrat Coalition, Secretary of the Congressional Black Caucus, and chair of the New Democrat Coalition National Security Taskforce.
Has served as campaign chair of the United Way of Pierce County, as a trustee of the Tacoma Public Library and Annie Wright Schools, and as a board member of Grand Cinema.
Lives in the district with her husband, according to her House website.
